title: My Rater and Writer Had Different Rules for Two Weeks

paragraphs: I built a pipeline that reads my git history and drafts blog posts for me. Part of it is a quality gate that auto-fails anything that sounds like AI wrote it. Necessary, given that AI is writing them.

For two weeks, the gate and the generator were working from different rule books. The generator read the rules from a canonical file on every run. The gate used a version I'd written from memory. They'd diverged before the first real pipeline ran.
Neither flagged anything. Caught it because one post sounded off when I read it out loud.
(Also: the pipeline required about 25 manual approval clicks per run before I sorted the permissions. Built automation, manually approved every step.)
Anyone else catch their quality gate scoring against different rules than the generator was using?
